content:
rachel: Heads-up: we're tightening write-push access to our container registry and rotating all registry tokens used by CI/CD. Details + required actions below.


tom: Need more context0why now?


rachel: We had a recent audit + a benign leak in a third-party script that used a registry token with broad push scope. Risk: image spoofing or malicious image push. So security is forcing least-privilege write tokens and automated rotation.


anil: What's changing exactly?


rachel: Summary: (1) Tokens that allow "push" to prod namespaces will be split into per-service "push:<repo>" tokens. (2) Default CI tokens will be read-only; write/push scopes must be requested with justification. (3) All existing push-capable tokens will be rotated and invalidated unless teams register them and confirm migration steps.


sec-bot: Inventory scan (2026-09-10 07:21 UTC): Found 28 tokens with wildcard push permissions (repo:*). Created tickets: SEC-9420..SEC-9427.


tom: Timeline? My deploys run every 2h, we can't break them.


rachel: Rollout plan: 
- 2026-09-17 00:00 UTC: New policy active for token creation (default read-only for CI).
- 2026-09-24 00:00 UTC: Backfill run to flag tokens with push:* and auto-create rotation tickets.
- 2026-10-01 00:00 UTC: Non-rotated push-capable tokens will be revoked.


anil: How do teams check which tokens they own?


rachel: Run: `registryctl tokens list --owner your-team --format csv` then grep for `push` scope. Example: 
```
registryctl tokens list --owner platform-team --format csv | grep push
# fields: id,owner,scopes,created_at,last_used
```
We will add a helper script in infra/tools that auto-opens a ticket with the token id and suggested scoped replacement.


tom: How should CI handle pushing images after change?


rachel: Options: 
1) Use per-repo push tokens scoped to the exact image repo. CI service accounts should request tokens via `registryctl tokens create --scope push:myorg/myrepo --ttl 30d --owner ci-team`.
2) Use ephemeral push creds via the OIDC flow: `registryctl oidc get-cred --repo myorg/myrepo --duration 1h` (recommended for ephemeral runners).
3) For monorepos that publish many images, create a deployment service identity with a narrow repo allowlist.


anil: What about DockerHub/GHPackages mirrors? Some runners push to mirrors.


rachel: Mirror accounts must also follow the same rules. If you have an external mirror that can't do OIDC, request a scoped machine token and add IP allowlist + narrow scope. Exceptions expire in 14 days by default.


registry-bot: Note: Related repos with embedded tokens detected: ci/build-scripts, infra/image-publish. Please rotate secrets and run `git-secrets --scan`.


tom: Will there be a migration helper? We have dozens of pipelines.


rachel: Yes0we're shipping a migration helper (`infra/tools/registry-migrate`) that will: 1) detect pipelines using wildcard push tokens, 2) propose per-repo token commands, 3) open SEC ticket with suggested new token id once rotation is complete. We'll publish usage in #eng-security.


anil: If a token is auto-rotated, how do we update pipeline configs atomically?


rachel: Recommended: use the helper to create the new token and update a secret in your secrets manager (Crossplane/HashiVault/GCP Secret Manager) in the same PR that updates pipeline config. We will allow a 48h staging overlap window for tokens created by the helper. For manual rotations please coordinate via the ticket.


sec-bot: Reminder: final warning scheduled 2026-09-30 00:00 UTC.


tom: Acknowledged. I'll run the `registryctl` audit today and open tickets for any critical pipelines.


rachel: Thanks. Office hours for token migration help: 2026-09-16 15:00 UTC in #eng-security. Paste `registryctl` outputs in the ticket.


registry-bot: Action: Created SEC-9428 for infra/image-publish with attached CSV.


anil: I'll start inventorying mirrors and runners and coordinate with infra.


rachel: Appreciate it. Ping me for any blocked flows so we can approve a short exception window. :thumbsup:
